---
# =============================================================================
# SCENARIO CATEGORY INDEX
# =============================================================================
#
# Central registry of scenario categories organized by data flow.
# Source of truth for:
#   - Canonical category and sub-category names
#   - Which persona roles each category applies to
#   - Which existing scenarios belong to which category
#   - Gold standard scenario tracking
#
# Data Flow (status quo — how therapy tracking works TODAY without the app):
#   Plan erstellen → Plan aushändigen → Plan ausfüllen →
#   Daten analysieren → Daten ablegen
#
# Naming convention (scenario folder names):
#   [action]_[object]_[qualifier]   (snake_case)
#   Variant suffix: __[qualifier]   (double underscore, only when same
#                                    persona has multiple of same category)
#
# Word standardization:
#   transfer (not handover/deliver) | protocol (not form/sheet)
#   capture (not dump/log)          | collaboratively (not with_client)
#   spontaneously (not at_night)    | data (not entries/information)
#
# Process for new scenarios:
#   1. Check if a matching category exists here
#   2. If not → define new sub-category, add to this index
#   3. Create scenario using canonical_name as folder name
#   4. Ensure other relevant personas are flagged for coverage
#
# Version: 1.3
# Created: 2026-02-06
# Updated: 2026-02-21
# Task: TASK-PROC-010-12, TASK-PROC-027-13, 2026-02-15_multi-category-cross-listing,
#   2026-02-21_update_user_flow_index
# Design document: requirements_tasks/process/AI_rules/requirements_management/
#   user_needs_structure/tasks/2026-02-05_explore_scenario_index_naming/
#   plans_and_protocols/2026-02-06_04_final_scenario_index.md
#
# Scenario Ideas:
#   The "ideas" section at the bottom of this file holds scenario ideas that
#   have been identified through brainstorming or flow analysis but have NOT
#   yet been written as full scenarios. Ideas are proposals for evaluation —
#   they may be promoted to real scenarios, merged with existing ones, or
#   discarded. An idea entry has: stage, category, description, suggested
#   personas, priority, and source. Ideas do NOT have scenario IDs.
#
# Technical / Multi-Persona Scenarios:
#   For purely technical scenarios (backup, migration, installation) where
#   the interaction is identical regardless of persona, a single scenario
#   can cover multiple personas. See README_4 "Technical / Multi-Persona
#   Scenarios" for rules. Such entries use multi_persona: true in YAML.
# =============================================================================

stages:

  # ===========================================================================
  # STAGE 1: PLAN CREATION (Planerstellung)
  # ===========================================================================

  - stage_id: creation
    display_name: "Plan Creation (Planerstellung)"
    description: >
      Designing and preparing structured tracking instruments — paper
      protocols, printed templates, self-designed journal pages — for
      therapy homework or personal use.
    categories:

      - id: "creation.prepare_protocol"
        canonical_name: "prepare_protocol_for_client"
        display_name: "Prepare Protocol for Client"
        description: >
          Therapist pulls a blank paper template from the filing cabinet,
          customizes it by hand for a specific client — writing margin
          notes, adding situation examples, adjusting columns. May also
          involve preparing verbal instructions or a sticky-note reminder
          for the session.
        applicable_roles:
          - role: therapist
            relevance: primary
          - role: self_user
            relevance: edge_case
            notes: "Self-user designing own paper tracking layout"
        instances:
          - persona_id: PERSONA-001
            persona_folder: dr_sarah
            scenario_id: SCEN-001-01
            scenario_folder: prepare_protocol_for_client
            outcome: success
            gold_status: true
            notes: "Paper anxiety protocol for Anna. Handwritten margin notes, customized columns."
          - persona_id: PERSONA-011
            persona_folder: prof_dr_weber
            scenario_id: SCEN-011-01
            scenario_folder: prepare_protocol_for_client
            outcome: success
            gold_status: false
            notes: "Free-form dream journal for Lena. Handwritten prompts on stationery, analog depth work meets digital compromise."
          - persona_id: PERSONA-012
            persona_folder: dr_med_turan
            scenario_id: SCEN-012-01
            scenario_folder: prepare_protocol_for_client
            outcome: success
            gold_status: false
            notes: "Medication-mood protocol for Herr Berger. SSRI→SNRI switch monitoring, photocopied form + KIS documentation, high time pressure."
        gaps:
          - role: self_user
            notes: "Self-user creating own paper tracking structure"

  # ===========================================================================
  # STAGE 2: PLAN DISTRIBUTION (Planübergabe)
  # ===========================================================================

  - stage_id: distribution
    display_name: "Plan Distribution (Planübergabe)"
    description: >
      Physically handing the paper protocol to the client during a session,
      explaining what to track, demonstrating how to fill it out, and
      addressing potential barriers (forgetting, privacy, motivation).
    categories:

      - id: "distribution.instruct_client"
        canonical_name: "instruct_client_on_protocol"
        display_name: "Instruct Client on Protocol"
        description: >
          Therapist hands the paper protocol to the client across the
          table, walks them through the columns, explains rating scales,
          discusses when and where to fill it out, and addresses concerns
          like "What if someone sees it?" or "What if I forget a day?"
          Currently embedded in Act 3 of SCEN-001-01 — may become
          standalone if the instruction/handover deserves its own story.
        applicable_roles:
          - role: therapist
            relevance: primary
          - role: client
            relevance: primary
            notes: "Client perspective: receiving paper, understanding instructions, feeling confident or overwhelmed"
        instances:
          - persona_id: PERSONA-002
            persona_folder: max_client
            scenario_id: SCEN-002-04
            scenario_folder: receive_protocol_homework
            outcome: partial
            gold_status: true
            notes: "Max receives Mood Protocol from Dr. Sarah. White Sheet Syndrome triggers, verbal instructions during cognitive depletion, fragile intention to start. Gold standard for client-side distribution."
          - persona_id: PERSONA-010
            persona_folder: sophie_structure_seeker
            scenario_id: SCEN-010-03
            scenario_folder: receive_protocol_homework
            outcome: partial
            gold_status: false
            notes: "Sophie receives Mood-and-Medication Protocol from Frau Kellner. ADHD hyperfocus creates elaborate Protocol Pocket system with three alarms, but sustainability uncertain. Object permanence drives visible storage."
          - persona_id: PERSONA-014
            persona_folder: jana_high_strung
            scenario_id: SCEN-014-03
            scenario_folder: receive_protocol_homework
            outcome: partial
            gold_status: false
            notes: "Jana receives Mood Protocol from Frau Albrecht. BPD volatility erasure fear (8→1→6 becomes '2'), DBT diary card shadow, accepts to maintain alliance but doubts format adequacy."
          - persona_id: PERSONA-009
            persona_folder: elias_skeptical_guardian
            scenario_id: SCEN-009-01
            scenario_folder: receive_protocol_homework
            outcome: partial
            gold_status: false
            notes: "Elias receives protocol from therapist. Social phobia privacy concerns (Krankenkasse discovery, partner finding form), Evidence Sheet Syndrome, storage crisis at home. Accepts reluctantly."
          - persona_id: PERSONA-015
            persona_folder: lena_depth_seeker
            scenario_id: SCEN-016-01
            scenario_folder: receive_protocol_homework
            outcome: partial
            gold_status: false
            notes: "Lena receives Dream & Experience Journal prompts from Prof. Dr. Weber. Handwritten stationery as transitional object, narrative invitation vs. structured form, grief-depth ambivalence, 3 AM capture dilemma, mother-in-law privacy threat."
          - persona_id: PERSONA-001
            persona_folder: dr_sarah
            scenario_id: SCEN-001-03
            scenario_folder: instruct_client_on_protocol
            outcome: success
            gold_status: true
            notes: "Dr. Sarah instructs Anna on Anxiety Protocol. Didactic handover: column-by-column explanation, barrier discussion (privacy, forgetting), psychoeducation approach. 10 min of session time. Gold standard for therapist-side distribution."
          - persona_id: PERSONA-011
            persona_folder: prof_dr_weber
            scenario_id: SCEN-011-03
            scenario_folder: instruct_client_on_protocol
            outcome: success
            gold_status: false
            notes: "Prof. Dr. Weber instructs Lena on Dream & Experience Journal. Ritual handover: handwritten stationery page as transitional object, 'invitation not homework' framing, phone concession as boundary-crossing. First time giving homework in a decade."
          - persona_id: PERSONA-012
            persona_folder: dr_med_turan
            scenario_id: SCEN-012-03
            scenario_folder: instruct_client_on_protocol
            outcome: success
            gold_status: false
            notes: "Dr. med. Turan instructs Herr Berger on Medication-Mood Protocol. 90-second medical handover: medication switch + protocol in under 4 min, safety net instruction, jacket-pocket moment. Expects 30% compliance."
        gaps: []

  # ===========================================================================
  # STAGE 3: DATA CAPTURE (Datenerfassung)
  # ===========================================================================

  - stage_id: capture
    display_name: "Data Capture (Datenerfassung)"
    description: >
      Recording mood, thoughts, symptoms, or behavioral data onto the
      paper protocol, into a phone notes app, a personal journal, or
      another analog/digital tool the persona currently uses. Varies
      by trigger (urgent vs. scheduled) and environment (dark bedroom,
      crowded train, kitchen table).
    categories:

      - id: "capture.spontaneous"
        canonical_name: "capture_data_spontaneously"
        display_name: "Capture Data Spontaneously"
        description: >
          Recording driven by internal urgency — racing thoughts at
          night, a sudden insight on the train, an emotional spike after
          a confrontation. The persona grabs whatever is available (paper
          notepad, phone notes app, napkin) under constraints: darkness,
          noise sensitivity, shaking hands, low cognitive capacity. The
          recording is reactive, not planned.
        applicable_roles:
          - role: client
            relevance: primary
          - role: self_user
            relevance: primary
        instances:
          - persona_id: PERSONA-002
            persona_folder: max_client
            scenario_id: SCEN-002-01
            scenario_folder: brain_dump_at_night
            outcome: failure
            gold_status: false
            notes: "Nighttime brain dump with paper notepad. Fails: dark room, pen noise, illegible handwriting, sleeping partner wakes."
        gaps:
          - role: client
            notes: "Other contexts: commute (scribbling on train), work break, waiting room"
          - role: self_user
            notes: "Same urgency pattern without therapy homework framing"

      - id: "capture.routine"
        canonical_name: "routine_data_entry"
        display_name: "Routine Data Entry"
        description: >
          Filling out the paper protocol as part of a daily or regular
          routine — after breakfast, before bed, or after specific events.
          The persona sits down with the form and a pen, tries to remember
          what happened, writes a number and maybe a sentence. Driven by
          habit or obligation, not emotional urgency. Risk of abandonment
          when motivation fades or the pen goes missing.
        applicable_roles:
          - role: client
            relevance: primary
          - role: self_user
            relevance: primary
        instances:
          - persona_id: PERSONA-002
            persona_folder: max_client
            scenario_id: SCEN-002-05
            scenario_folder: routine_data_entry
            outcome: partial
            gold_status: false
            notes: "Wednesday evening kitchen table entry. Wall of Awful initiation delay, 'nothing happened' paralysis, retroactive fabrication for missed Mon/Tue, Notes column skipped. 18 min for 3 rows."
        gaps:
          - role: client
            notes: "Other client archetypes: ADHD routine decay, anxiety perfectionism trap"
          - role: self_user
            notes: "Daily self-tracking with journal, phone notes, or paper log"

  # ===========================================================================
  # STAGE 4: DATA ANALYSIS (Datenanalyse)
  # ===========================================================================

  - stage_id: analysis
    display_name: "Data Analysis (Datenanalyse)"
    description: >
      Reviewing tracked data — alone or together with the therapist.
      Includes the client's pre-session preparation (re-reading their
      own paper entries), transporting the physical protocol to the
      practice, the collaborative review on the table between therapist
      and client, and solitary self-reflection for those without a
      therapist.
    categories:

      - id: "analysis.prepare_for_session"
        canonical_name: "prepare_for_therapy_session"
        display_name: "Prepare for Therapy Session"
        description: >
          The night before or morning of the session, the client sits
          down with their filled paper protocol and tries to reconstruct
          what happened that week. Reads terse entries ("Mood 3") and
          struggles to recall context. Confronts illegible handwriting
          from bad days, empty rows from days they didn't track, and
          the shame of incomplete homework. Tries to identify talking
          points so they don't sit in the therapist's chair saying
          "I don't remember."
        applicable_roles:
          - role: client
            relevance: primary
          - role: therapist
            relevance: secondary
            notes: "Therapist reviewing notes from previous session to prepare"
        instances:
          - persona_id: PERSONA-002
            persona_folder: max_client
            scenario_id: SCEN-002-03
            scenario_folder: prepare_for_therapy_session
            outcome: partial
            gold_status: true
            notes: "Sunday evening review at kitchen table. Context loss, illegible Thursday, 3 blank days, shame. Arrives with fragments."
          - persona_id: PERSONA-014
            persona_folder: jana_high_strung
            scenario_id: SCEN-014-01
            scenario_folder: prepare_for_therapy_session
            outcome: partial
            gold_status: false
            notes: "Wednesday evening bedroom review. BPD volatility erasure (8→1→6 becomes '2'), emotional re-activation, scattered data in texts/voice memos, 5 blank days."
          - persona_id: PERSONA-010
            persona_folder: sophie_structure_seeker
            scenario_id: SCEN-010-02
            scenario_folder: prepare_for_therapy_session
            outcome: partial
            gold_status: false
            notes: "Tuesday evening desk review. ADHD object permanence failure, data fragmented across 5 systems, hyperfocus trap (14-min detour), 28% completion, system decay cycle."
          - persona_id: PERSONA-015
            persona_folder: lena_depth_seeker
            scenario_id: SCEN-016-02
            scenario_folder: prepare_for_therapy_session
            outcome: partial
            gold_status: false
            notes: "Sunday evening bedroom review. Non-sequential affect-led scan of dream journal + phone notes. Split media, motif tracking by feel not search, pre-processing risk, medium hierarchy guilt, pencil-dot selection for session."
        gaps: []

      - id: "analysis.transfer_to_therapist"
        canonical_name: "transfer_data_to_therapist"
        display_name: "Transfer Data to Therapist"
        description: >
          The client must physically bring the paper protocol to the
          therapy session. This means remembering the object exists,
          locating it (desk? bag? shoe rack?), putting it in a bag,
          and not losing it on the commute. The handover moment in the
          session — pulling the paper from the bag and placing it on
          the table — carries emotional weight: proof of effort, or
          the shame of arriving empty-handed.
        applicable_roles:
          - role: client
            relevance: primary
        instances:
          - persona_id: PERSONA-002
            persona_folder: max_client
            scenario_id: SCEN-002-02
            scenario_folder: forgotten_protocol_transfer
            outcome: failure
            gold_status: true
            notes: "Protocol on shoe rack at home. Panicked reconstruction from phone notes on S-Bahn. 30% of session wasted. Gold standard for failure outcome variant."
          - persona_id: PERSONA-010
            persona_folder: sophie_structure_seeker
            scenario_id: SCEN-010-01
            scenario_folder: successful_protocol_handover
            outcome: success
            gold_status: true
            notes: "Protocol Pocket in tote bag. 4/7 days filled. Ceremonial handover. Frau Kellner finds medication-mood correlation. Gold standard for success outcome variant."
          - persona_id: PERSONA-014
            persona_folder: jana_high_strung
            scenario_id: SCEN-014-02
            scenario_folder: transfer_data_to_therapist
            outcome: partial
            gold_status: false
            notes: "Diary arrives but single-number format erases BPD volatility. 'Mood 2' is average of 8→1→6. 7-second voice memo more useful than 3 days of entries. Medium distorts message."
          - persona_id: PERSONA-015
            persona_folder: lena_depth_seeker
            scenario_id: SCEN-016-03
            scenario_folder: forgotten_protocol_transfer
            outcome: failure
            gold_status: false
            notes: "Dream journal notebook left on nightstand. Phone has partial entries (garden association) but not primary material. Session proceeds at reduced depth — verbal reconstruction strips 3 AM texture. Contrast: Max forgets structured data (numbers reconstructable), Lena forgets narrative language (irreproducible)."
          - persona_id: PERSONA-015
            persona_folder: lena_depth_seeker
            scenario_id: SCEN-016-04
            scenario_folder: successful_protocol_handover
            outcome: success
            gold_status: false
            notes: "Dream journal arrives. Lena reads marked entries aloud, 3 AM voice intact. Cross-session motif emerges (corridor→kitchen→garden, obstacles shrinking). Split media (notebook + phone) creates complete arc. Success despite fragile transfer chain and manual pattern tracking."
          - persona_id: PERSONA-009
            persona_folder: elias_skeptical_guardian
            scenario_id: SCEN-009-02
            scenario_folder: transfer_data_to_therapist
            outcome: partial
            gold_status: false
            notes: "Anxiety Protocol arrives but data is degraded: public logging barrier → shadow accounting → approximated numbers. Lies of omission hide real reason for gaps. Also covers analysis.review_collaboratively (handover and in-session review in same moment)."
        gaps:
          - role: client
            notes: "Other failure modes: paper damaged (rain, coffee), wrong week grabbed, self-censored entries"

      - id: "analysis.review_collaboratively"
        canonical_name: "review_data_collaboratively"
        display_name: "Review Data Collaboratively"
        description: >
          Therapist and client sit across from each other with the paper
          protocol unfolded on the table between them. The therapist
          scans rows of handwritten numbers, squints at illegible entries,
          asks "Tell me about this day." They identify patterns together —
          but it's slow: no graphs, no sorting, just manual row-by-row
          scanning. Comparing this week to last week requires finding
          last week's paper (if it wasn't lost). The therapist
          transcribes key observations to their own notepad by hand.
        applicable_roles:
          - role: therapist
            relevance: primary
            notes: "Drives the analysis, asks probing questions, identifies clinical patterns"
          - role: client
            relevance: primary
            notes: "Participates, provides context behind entries, gains self-awareness"
        instances:
          - persona_id: PERSONA-001
            persona_folder: dr_sarah
            scenario_id: SCEN-001-02
            scenario_folder: review_protocol_with_client
            outcome: success
            gold_status: true
            notes: "Reviews Anna's anxiety protocol on table. Spots anticipatory anxiety pattern. Data quality concern (batch-written entries)."
          - persona_id: PERSONA-011
            persona_folder: prof_dr_weber
            scenario_id: SCEN-011-02
            scenario_folder: review_data_collaboratively
            outcome: success
            gold_status: false
            notes: "Reviews Lena's dream journal entries together. Notebook + phone entries read aloud. Associative exploration: corridor dream → grandmother's hallway."
          - persona_id: PERSONA-012
            persona_folder: dr_med_turan
            scenario_id: SCEN-012-02
            scenario_folder: review_data_collaboratively
            outcome: success
            gold_status: false
            notes: "Reviews Herr Berger's medication protocol at 4-week follow-up. Crumpled paper, 39% complete, coffee stain obscures days 2-3. 90-second clinical scan, dose decision with partial data."
          # Cross-listed from analysis.transfer_to_therapist
          # These client-perspective scenarios cover both handover AND collaborative review
          # in the same session moment. Primary category: analysis.transfer_to_therapist.
          - persona_id: PERSONA-010
            persona_folder: sophie_structure_seeker
            scenario_id: SCEN-010-01
            scenario_folder: successful_protocol_handover
            outcome: success
            gold_status: false
            cross_listed_from: "analysis.transfer_to_therapist"
            notes: "Cross-listed: Sophie's ceremonial handover includes Frau Kellner identifying medication-mood correlation — handover and collaborative review are one session moment."
          - persona_id: PERSONA-014
            persona_folder: jana_high_strung
            scenario_id: SCEN-014-02
            scenario_folder: transfer_data_to_therapist
            outcome: partial
            gold_status: false
            cross_listed_from: "analysis.transfer_to_therapist"
            notes: "Cross-listed: Jana's handover includes Frau Albrecht's review moment — BPD volatility erasure discovered when therapist sees 'Mood 2' on the table."
          - persona_id: PERSONA-015
            persona_folder: lena_depth_seeker
            scenario_id: SCEN-016-04
            scenario_folder: successful_protocol_handover
            outcome: success
            gold_status: false
            cross_listed_from: "analysis.transfer_to_therapist"
            notes: "Cross-listed: Lena reads marked dream entries aloud to Prof. Dr. Weber — handover immediately transitions into deep collaborative review, cross-session motif emerges."
          - persona_id: PERSONA-009
            persona_folder: elias_skeptical_guardian
            scenario_id: SCEN-009-02
            scenario_folder: transfer_data_to_therapist
            outcome: partial
            gold_status: false
            cross_listed_from: "analysis.transfer_to_therapist"
            notes: "Cross-listed: Dr. Hofmann reads numbers aloud, identifies downward trend, proposes next exercise — client-perspective collaborative review on degraded data. Unique: therapist interprets data the client knows is inaccurate."
        gaps: []

      - id: "analysis.self_reflect"
        canonical_name: "self_review_and_reflect"
        display_name: "Self-Review and Reflect"
        description: >
          A person without a therapist (or between sessions) sits down
          with their journal, notebook, or phone notes and tries to see
          patterns in their own entries. Flips through pages, tries to
          compare last week to this week, maybe tallies numbers on a
          scrap of paper. No one is guiding the review — they must
          figure out what matters on their own. Insights are hard to
          find without visualization; the data is scattered across
          pages and dates.
        applicable_roles:
          - role: self_user
            relevance: primary
          - role: client
            relevance: secondary
            notes: "Client reviewing data between sessions for personal understanding"
        instances: []
        gaps:
          - role: self_user
            notes: "Core self-user scenario: reviewing own journal/notes for mood trends"
          - role: client
            notes: "Mid-week independent review — not pre-session prep, just personal curiosity"

  # ===========================================================================
  # STAGE 5: DATA MANAGEMENT (Datenverwaltung)
  # ===========================================================================

  - stage_id: management
    display_name: "Data Management (Datenverwaltung)"
    description: >
      Long-term handling of tracked data using current tools: storing
      filled paper protocols in folders or drawers, photocopying pages
      before handing them to the therapist, dealing with accumulated
      stacks of old forms, or losing weeks of data when a notebook
      gets damaged or thrown away.
    categories:

      - id: "management.archive_and_retrieve"
        canonical_name: "archive_and_retrieve_data"
        display_name: "Archive and Retrieve Data"
        description: >
          Deciding what to do with completed paper protocols after
          the therapy session. Filing them in a folder at home, stuffing
          them in a drawer, or losing them in the recycling. Weeks later,
          wanting to look back at old entries and either finding the
          stack or discovering it's gone. The therapist may keep their
          own copies in the patient file — but the client rarely has
          access to those.
        applicable_roles:
          - role: client
            relevance: primary
            notes: "Managing own paper archive at home"
          - role: therapist
            relevance: secondary
            notes: "Filing client protocols in patient records"
          - role: self_user
            relevance: primary
            notes: "Managing personal journal/notebook archive"
        instances: []
        gaps:
          - role: client
            notes: "Client trying to find old protocols for long-term comparison"
          - role: self_user
            notes: "Self-user managing growing stack of notebooks/notes"

      - id: "management.share_externally"
        canonical_name: "share_data_externally"
        display_name: "Share Data Externally"
        description: >
          Sharing tracked data with someone other than the primary
          therapist — a psychiatrist who needs medication compliance
          data, an insurance company requesting documentation, a new
          therapist after switching practices, or a family member who
          wants to understand. Currently means photocopying paper
          forms, transcribing handwritten entries into an email, or
          physically carrying the folder to another office.
        applicable_roles:
          - role: client
            relevance: primary
            notes: "Sharing with psychiatrist, insurance, new therapist"
          - role: therapist
            relevance: secondary
            notes: "Providing summaries for referrals or insurance"
          - role: self_user
            relevance: primary
            notes: "Sharing with a doctor, coach, or trusted person"
        instances: []
        gaps:
          - role: client
            notes: "Client needing to share history with new provider"
          - role: self_user
            notes: "Self-user showing data to a doctor or partner"

      - id: "management.preservation"
        canonical_name: "protect_data_from_loss"
        display_name: "Protect Data from Loss"
        description: >
          Safeguarding tracked data against accidental loss caused by
          device failure, theft, physical damage, or platform migration.
          Unlike archive_and_retrieve (intentional filing of completed
          data), preservation addresses emergency recovery and continuity:
          recovering after device loss or theft, migrating data to a new
          phone or system, and maintaining data integrity across platform
          changes. Status quo: paper users rely on fireproof safes or
          scanning into practice management software; notes-app users
          depend on OS backup (iCloud, Google Drive) often without
          explicit intent; hybrid users store scans in cloud folders.
        applicable_roles:
          - role: client
            relevance: primary
            notes: "Fears losing weeks of tracking data with a lost phone or damaged notebook"
          - role: self_user
            relevance: primary
            notes: "No therapist backup copy — personal data exists in one place only"
          - role: therapist
            relevance: secondary
            notes: "Therapist copies in patient file provide partial backup for clinical data"
        instances: []
        gaps:
          - role: client
            notes: "Device loss/theft recovery; migration to new phone; paper damage (water, fire)"
          - role: self_user
            notes: "Long-term storage of completed tracking cycles without therapist file as safety net"

      - id: "management.destruction"
        canonical_name: "destroy_data_intentionally"
        display_name: "Intentional Data Destruction"
        description: >
          Deliberately eliminating tracked data — shredding paper
          protocols, deleting app entries, or ritually disposing of
          journals. Distinct from archive_and_retrieve (which preserves
          data) and from routine editing (which modifies content).

          employer), shame (ripping out pages documenting distressing
          episodes), or therapeutic closure (end of therapy, closing a

          or total (wiping everything). Status quo: paper users tear
          pages, shred documents, or burn notebooks; digital users
          delete apps or clear entries.
        applicable_roles:
          - role: client
            relevance: primary
            notes: "Privacy panic, shame-driven deletion, end-of-therapy disposal"
          - role: self_user
            relevance: primary
            notes: "Same emotional triggers without therapist guidance on data retention"
        instances: []
        gaps:
          - role: client
            notes: "Panic deletion (Elias pattern), selective shame removal (Jana pattern), therapeutic closure ritual"
          - role: self_user
            notes: "Self-directed disposal decisions without clinical guidance"

  # ===========================================================================
  # STAGE 6: INTERVENTION (Krisenunterstützung)
  # ===========================================================================
  #
  # Unlike the linear data flow (creation → distribution → capture →
  # analysis → management), intervention is triggered by emotional state,
  # not by a process step. The user consults pre-prepared support materials
  # rather than recording data.
  #
  # Decision: New top-level stage (not sub-category of existing stage).
  # Rationale: See plans_and_protocols/2026-02-14_01_protocol_category_definitions.md
  # ===========================================================================

  - stage_id: intervention
    display_name: "Intervention (Krisenunterstützung)"
    description: >
      Consulting or following pre-prepared support materials during
      moments of distress or crisis. Unlike the linear data flow
      (creation → distribution → capture → analysis → management),
      intervention is triggered by emotional state, not by a step in
      the tracking process. The materials consulted are not filled out
      by the user but read, followed, or activated: skill cards with
      coping techniques, safety plan instructions, emergency contact
      lists, or positive resources (hope box, uplifting images).
    categories:

      - id: "intervention.coping"
        canonical_name: "access_coping_resources"
        display_name: "Access Coping Resources"
        description: >
          Reaching for pre-prepared coping materials during emotional
          distress — pulling a DBT skill card from a wallet, opening
          a list of grounding techniques, looking at uplifting photos
          in a hope box, or re-reading self-soothing instructions.
          The user is not recording data but consulting materials to
          regulate their emotional state. Access barriers matter:
          finding the card in a dark room, reading small print through
          tears, locating the right technique among many. Includes
          both active coping techniques (breathing exercises, skill
          chains) and passive resources (hope box, motivational images).
        applicable_roles:
          - role: client
            relevance: primary
            notes: "Accessing therapist-curated skill cards, coping lists during distress episodes"
          - role: self_user
            relevance: primary
            notes: "Same need but without therapist-curated materials — must find own resources"
        instances: []
        gaps:
          - role: client
            notes: "DBT skill card access in crisis, hope box consultation, grounding technique lookup"
          - role: self_user
            notes: "Self-assembled coping resource access without clinical curation"

      - id: "intervention.safety"
        canonical_name: "follow_safety_protocol"
        display_name: "Follow Safety Protocol"
        description: >
          Consulting emergency instructions during acute crisis —
          following a safety plan when suicidal ideation intensifies,
          calling a crisis line listed on a card, or acting on
          medication side-effect instructions ("Call the practice
          immediately if..."). Unlike coping resources (which help
          regulate distress), safety protocols are binary action
          sequences with specific triggers and defined steps. The
          material must be immediately findable, unambiguous, and
          actionable under extreme cognitive impairment. Status quo:
          printed cards carried in wallets, safety plans taped to
          fridges, emergency numbers in phone contacts.
        applicable_roles:
          - role: client
            relevance: primary
            notes: "Following therapist-provided safety plans and emergency instructions"
          - role: self_user
            relevance: secondary
            notes: "Self-created safety plans based on self-help resources"
        instances: []
        gaps:
          - role: client
            notes: "Suicidal crisis safety plan activation, medication emergency response"
          - role: self_user
            notes: "Self-directed safety plan without clinical oversight"

  # ===========================================================================
  # STAGE 7: PLAN MODIFICATION (Plananpassung)
  # ===========================================================================
  #
  # Distinct from creation (designing from scratch): modification starts
  # from a working instrument and alters it based on experience.
  #
  # Gemini suggested "adaptation" — rejected in favor of "modification"
  # (matches noun style of other stages: creation, distribution, etc.).
  # Rationale: See plans_and_protocols/2026-02-14_01_protocol_category_definitions.md
  # ===========================================================================

  - stage_id: modification
    display_name: "Plan Modification (Plananpassung)"
    description: >
      Adjusting an existing tracking protocol that is already in use —
      adding or removing columns, rewording questions, changing rating
      scales, or abandoning sections that don't work. Distinct from
      creation (designing a protocol from scratch) in that modification
      starts from a working instrument and alters it based on
      experience. Modifications may be collaborative (adjusted together
      in session) or autonomous (client adapts alone between sessions).
    categories:

      - id: "modification.collaborative"
        canonical_name: "modify_protocol_collaboratively"
        display_name: "Modify Protocol Collaboratively"
        description: >
          Therapist and client adjust the tracking protocol together
          during a therapy session — crossing out a column that doesn't
          work, adding a new one based on emerging patterns, rewording
          a confusing question, or simplifying the rating scale. The
          paper form gets annotated: margins filled with corrections,
          arrows pointing to new sections, sticky-note addenda. The
          trigger is typically a pattern noticed during collaborative
          review (analysis.review_collaboratively) that reveals the
          current format is inadequate. Status quo: handwritten
          amendments on the physical form, or printing a revised
          version for next week.
        applicable_roles:
          - role: therapist
            relevance: primary
            notes: "Drives the modification based on clinical judgment; may redesign between sessions"
          - role: client
            relevance: primary
            notes: "Participates in session, suggests changes based on lived experience"
        instances: []
        gaps:
          - role: therapist
            notes: "In-session annotation, between-session redesign, iterative refinement over weeks"
          - role: client
            notes: "Client-initiated suggestions ('This column stresses me out')"

      - id: "modification.autonomous"
        canonical_name: "modify_protocol_autonomously"
        display_name: "Modify Protocol Autonomously"
        description: >
          Client or self-user alters their tracking protocol alone,
          without therapist involvement — covering a stressful column
          with tape, inventing personal shorthand to speed up entry,
          stopping certain rows by decision or frustration, adding
          categories the therapist didn't include. These modifications
          may be adaptive (improving the tool for personal needs) or
          avoidant (eliminating uncomfortable tracking). The therapist
          may discover the changes only when the modified form arrives
          at the next session. Status quo: physical alterations to
          paper (crossing out, taping over, adding sticky notes) or
          simply ignoring sections.
        applicable_roles:
          - role: client
            relevance: primary
            notes: "Adapting therapist-provided protocol to personal needs or avoiding difficult sections"
          - role: self_user
            relevance: primary
            notes: "Iterating on self-designed tracking structure without external guidance"
        instances: []
        gaps:
          - role: client
            notes: "Adaptive modification (personal shorthand) vs. avoidant modification (skipping painful columns)"
          - role: self_user
            notes: "Continuous iteration on tracking structure without therapist feedback loop"

  # ===========================================================================
  # STAGE 8: TEMPLATE SHARING (Vorlagenaustausch)
  # ===========================================================================
  #
  # About sharing/discovering the BLUEPRINT (template structure), not
  # the FILLED DATA. Distinct from management.share_externally (which
  # shares filled data with third parties).

  - stage_id: sharing
    display_name: "Template Sharing (Vorlagenaustausch)"
    description: >
      Sharing or discovering tracking template blueprints — the
      structure of what to track, when, how, and why — rather than
      filled-out data. Therapists copy templates from therapy manuals,
      share approaches with colleagues, or adapt published worksheets.
      Clients and self-users discover tracking structures in self-help
      books, apps, or online communities. This stage is about the
      blueprint, not the data recorded in it.
    categories:

      - id: "sharing.peer_exchange"
        canonical_name: "share_template_with_peer"
        display_name: "Share Template with Peer"
        description: >
          Therapist shares a tracking template with a colleague —
          photocopying a protocol from a therapy manual, emailing a
          Word template, explaining a custom tracking approach during
          supervision or Intervision. The recipient adapts the template
          for their own clients. Status quo: photocopying from published
          CBT/DBT manuals, sharing Word files via email, verbal
          descriptions during case conferences. No standardized format
          for template exchange.
        applicable_roles:
          - role: therapist
            relevance: primary
            notes: "Sharing template designs with colleagues, trainees, or supervisees"
        instances: []
        gaps:
          - role: therapist
            notes: "Dr. Sarah (PERSONA-001): persona mentions Word templates and PiA cluster but does not capture peer sharing need"

      - id: "sharing.independent_discovery"
        canonical_name: "discover_template_independently"
        display_name: "Discover Template Independently"
        description: >
          Person searches for a suitable tracking structure without
          therapist guidance — browsing self-help books for mood diary
          formats, downloading templates from apps or websites, asking
          in online communities what others track and how. Driven by
          the need to start tracking without knowing what to track or
          how to structure it. The challenge is evaluating quality and
          relevance without clinical guidance. Status quo: Ratgeber
          books, mental health apps (Daylio, Moodpath), online forums,
          trial and error.
        applicable_roles:
          - role: self_user
            relevance: primary
            notes: "Must find tracking structure without therapist — high urgency"
          - role: client
            relevance: secondary
            notes: "May seek supplementary templates beyond what therapist provides"
        instances: []
        gaps:
          - role: self_user
            notes: "Lisa (PERSONA-005): template discovery need not explicit in persona; David (PERSONA-008): system-hopping frames discovery as problem, not need"

---

### LÜCKE 1: Die Welt der Self-User (ohne therapeutisches Netz)

Diese Personas kämpfen komplett allein. Ihre Motivation und ihre Fehlschläge sehen völlig anders aus als die der Therapie-Klienten.

**1. Lisa (The Waitlist Bridger)**
*   **Szenario:** *The "Proof of Illness" GP Visit* (`management.share_externally` / `analysis.self_reflect`)
*   **Story:** Lisa hat nach 6 Monaten Wartezeit einen Termin beim Hausarzt, um ihre Krankschreibung oder Überweisung zu verlängern. Sie will *beweisen*, dass sie wirklich depressiv ist. Sie blättert panisch durch ihr Zettelchaos, um Muster zu finden, merkt aber, dass ihre Notizen ("heute nur geweint") nicht "medizinisch genug" wirken, um ernst genommen zu werden. Sie fühlt sich wie eine Hochstaplerin.
*   **Out-of-the-Box Value:** Zeigt, dass Daten für Self-User oft als **Legitimation gegenüber dem System** dienen, nicht nur zur Selbsterkenntnis.

**2. Michael (The High-Performer)**
*   **Szenario:** *The Missing Link (Wearable vs. Psyche)* (`capture.routine` / `analysis.self_reflect`)
*   **Story:** Michael schaut auf seine Garmin-Uhr: "Body Battery 15, Stresslevel hoch". Er versteht nicht, warum. Er hat 8 Stunden im Bett gelegen, hatte gestern keinen Sport. Was die Uhr nicht weiß: Er hatte gestern einen extrem toxischen Call mit seinem Chef und hat danach 3 Bier getrunken. Da er Emotionen nicht trackt (zu esoterisch), fehlen ihm die Daten, um den physischen Absturz zu erklären.
*   **Out-of-the-Box Value:** Der Kampf gegen "Daten-Silos". Körperdaten ohne mentale Metadaten sind oft nutzlos.

**3. David (The Structure Seeker)**
*   **Szenario:** *The Graveyard of Good Intentions* (`sharing.independent_discovery` / `capture.routine`)
*   **Story:** David lädt seine 21. Habit-Tracker-App herunter. Im Hyperfokus baut er 15 Gewohnheiten auf ("Wasser trinken, Meds, Lesen, Mood, Journaling"). Tag 1-3 sind perfekt. Tag 4: Er vergisst es morgens. Am Abend sieht er den gebrochenen "Streak" in der App. Das rote X demotiviert ihn so sehr, dass er die App sofort löscht.
*   **Out-of-the-Box Value:** Zeigt das "Toxic Streak" Problem. Gamification, die bei Neurotypischen funktioniert, zerstört bei ADHS das System komplett.

**4. Hanna (The Sleepless)**
*   **Szenario:** *The Absolute Dark Brain Dump* (`capture.spontaneous`)
*   **Story:** Hanna wacht um 3 Uhr nachts auf. Das Gedankenkarussell dreht sich. Sie MUSS die Gedanken auslagern. Aber ihr Partner schläft 30 cm neben ihr. Sie darf kein Licht anmachen, sie kann nicht aufstehen (kalter Boden = endgültig wach). Sie versucht, im Stockdunkeln auf einen Block zu schreiben. Am nächsten Morgen kann sie das Gekritzel nicht lesen.
*   **Out-of-the-Box Value:** Im Gegensatz zu Max (Depression), bei dem es um Antrieb geht, ist Hannas Problem rein physikalisch/umgebungsbedingt (absolute Licht- und Geräuschempfindlichkeit).

**5. Nina (The Energy Budgeter)**
*   **Szenario:** *The 72-Hour PEM Lag* (`analysis.self_reflect`)
*   **Story:** Nina (Long-COVID) wacht an einem Samstag mit einem totalen Crash (Post-Exertional Malaise) auf. Sie kann nicht aufstehen. Sie versucht herauszufinden, was sie falsch gemacht hat. Das Problem: Der Auslöser war nicht am Freitag, sondern ein 15-minütiges Telefonat am *Mittwoch*. Mit ihrem aktuellen Papiertagebuch sieht sie diese zeitverzögerten Zusammenhänge nicht.
*   **Out-of-the-Box Value:** Tracking von extrem zeitverzögerten Reaktionen (Lag), bei denen einfache Ursache-Wirkung-Darstellungen (gleicher Tag) versagen.

---

### LÜCKE 2: Die Krisen- und Sicherheits-Layer (Intervention)

Wir haben das Thema "Datenerfassung" gut abgedeckt, aber was passiert im absoluten Ernstfall?

**6. Jana (The High-Strung)**
*   **Szenario:** *The Blind Panic Skill Search* (`intervention.coping`)
*   **Story:** Jana triggert in einen BPD-Rage-State. Die Anspannung schießt auf 9/10. Sie *will* einen DBT-Skill anwenden (Eiswürfel, Atemtechnik). Ihre Therapeutin hat ihr eine laminierte Skill-Karte gegeben. Jana wühlt weinend in ihrer Tasche, findet die Karte nicht, ihre Hände zittern, ihr Tunnelblick verhindert, dass sie die kleine Schrift lesen kann. Sie gibt auf und greift zu selbstverletzendem Verhalten.
*   **Out-of-the-Box Value:** Das System muss im Panik-Zustand bedienbar sein. Wenn man 5 Klicks braucht, um an einen Notfall-Skill zu kommen, ist die App im Ernstfall nutzlos.

**7. Dr. Turan (The Rapid Monitor)**
*   **Szenario:** *The Unused Emergency Plan* (`intervention.safety`)
*   **Story:** Turan erfährt im Follow-Up, dass Herr Berger vor zwei Wochen massive, gefährliche Unruhezustände (SNRI-Nebenwirkung) hatte. Turan fragt entsetzt: "Warum haben Sie nicht sofort angerufen? Das stand doch unten auf dem Protokoll!" Berger antwortet: "Das Protokoll lag zu Hause, und ich war auf der Arbeit. Ich wollte nicht stören."
*   **Out-of-the-Box Value:** Der Therapeut verlässt sich auf eine Sicherheitsanweisung (Krisenschutz), die an ein physisches Medium gebunden ist, das im entscheidenden Moment nicht verfügbar ist.

---

### LÜCKE 3: Lifecycle, Management & Privacy Extreme

Was passiert mit den Daten, wenn die Woche vorbei ist?

**8. Elias (The Skeptical Guardian)**
*   **Szenario:** *The Panic Delete* (`management.destruction`)
*   **Story:** Elias sitzt im Wohnzimmer. Sein Partner nimmt kurz Elias' Handy, um ein Rezept zu googeln. Elias sieht, dass die Notizen-App (mit seinen Social-Phobia-Einträgen) noch im Hintergrund im App-Switcher offen ist. In einem Anflug von Panik reißt er dem Partner das Handy aus der Hand und löscht blind die gesamte App oder den gesamten Ordner. Wochenlange harte Arbeit ist weg, nur um die Fassade zu wahren.
*   **Out-of-the-Box Value:** Datenschutz bedeutet hier nicht Verschlüsselung gegen Hacker, sondern der sofortige Schutz vor dem Menschen, der auf dem gleichen Sofa sitzt (Intimate Intruder). Braucht einen "Panic Flip" oder "Tarnkappen-Modus".

**9. Dr. Sarah (The Structured VT Professional)**
*   **Szenario:** *The Friday Night Gutachten* (`analysis.therapist_solo`)
*   **Story:** Dr. Sarah muss freitagabends einen Gutachterbericht für die Krankenkasse schreiben, um 20 weitere Therapiestunden für Anna zu beantragen. Sie hat 15 zerknitterte, handschriftliche Wochenprotokolle vor sich liegen. Sie muss manuell zählen, wie oft Panikattacken auftraten und ob die durchschnittliche Angstkurve sinkt. Es dauert zwei Stunden, sie hasst diesen Teil ihres Jobs abgrundtief.
*   **Out-of-the-Box Value:** Therapeuten nutzen die Daten nicht nur *mit* dem Patienten (wie in SCEN-001-02), sondern auch *alleine* für bürokratische Überlebenskämpfe. Eine Export/Aggregations-Funktion wäre hier Gold wert.

**10. System/Maintenance Persona**
*   **Szenario:** *The Silent OS Update Corruption* (`management.preservation`)
*   **Story:** Ein Nutzer kauft ein neues Handy. Die Datenmigration vom alten aufs neue Handy läuft durchs OS (iCloud/Google). Er öffnet seine Notizen-App, in der er 2 Jahre Therapie dokumentiert hat – aber durch ein Format-Update sind alle Datumsstempel zerschossen und Tabellen verrutscht. Die therapeutische Historie ist ein unlesbarer Brei.
*   **Out-of-the-Box Value:** Technische Resilienz. Wenn die App rein lokal ist, MUSS der Umzug auf ein neues Gerät manipulationssicher von der App selbst gemanagt werden, da sonst Lebenskrisen-Daten verloren gehen.

---

### Wie sollen wir vorgehen?

Wir haben das Budget und die Systematik, um diese Lücken extrem präzise zu füllen. 

Ich empfehle folgendes Vorgehen:
1. **Prio A:** Wir erstellen 1-2 Master-Szenarien für die komplett vernachlässigten Self-User (z.B. **Lisa's Hausarzt-Besuch** und **David's Habit-Graveyard**).
2. **Prio B:** Wir erstellen die beiden Interventions-Szenarien (**Jana's Panic Search** und **Dr. Turans Unused Safety Plan**), da wir im Flow-Index bereits gesehen haben, dass der "Crisis Response Flow" massiv blockiert ist.
3. **Prio C:** Wir decken die "Panic Delete" (Elias) und "Gutachten" (Dr. Sarah) Ränder ab.
